 Judgment

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident happened on 29-04-2013 at about 4.15 p.m.
2.

The brief facts of the petition averments are as under:
On the above said date and time, the petitioner was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-U-2463 on left side of the road from Bellandur towards Marathahalli slowly and cautiously by observing all traffic rules and regulations.
When he was proceeding near Kadubisanahalli fly over, at that time, the driver of the car bearing No.KA-03- AA-1996 came in a rash and negligent manner, without following traffic rules and regulations and came in opposite direction on one way and suddenly took right turn without observing movements of the vehicles and dashed to the SCH-16 petitioner motor cycle, because of which the petitioner sustained communited fracture of left 3rd metacarpal, laceration left index finger, abrasions all over the body.
He was immediately admitted to VIMS Hospital, wherein first aid was given.

Thereafter, he admitted as an inpatient from 29- 04-2013 to 01-05-2013,
during the said period, the petitioner underwent ORIF left 3rd metacarpal and wound debridement and suturing of index finger.
The petitioner was discharged with an advice of follow up treatment.
3. It is further case of the petitioner that, he has spent considerable amount towards his treatment and he has to bear other expenses for removal of implants.
It is stated that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and partner at Chef Baker's at Doddnekkundi, Bangalore and earning Rs.50,000/- per month.
Due to the impact of the said accident, the petitioner became permanently disabled and not able to earn anything.
The jurisdictional police have registered a case against the driver of the above said offending car in their Crime No.46/2013 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
The first respondent being the owner of the above said car and second respondent being SCH-16 the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, prayed to allow the petition.
4. In response to the notice, the second respondent appeared, whereas first respondent was placed exparte, as he failed to appear before the court in spite of service of notice.
5. The respondent No.2 admitted that, it had issued policy in respect of car bearing No.KA-03-AA-1996 and it was valid from 16-02-2013 to 15-02-2014.
The respondent No.2 denied the age, income and occupation of the petitioner and also the manner of accident.
The respondent No.2 contended that, the driver of the above said car was not holding valid and effective driving licence and was not qualified for holding such a driving licence.
The owner of the said vehicle has been knowing fully handed over the position of the said vehicle to the driver who did not possessed valid and effective driving licence.

It is contended that, the driver of the above said car was in the Sri Gnanashekar M.S.P vs M/S. Suhalaya Travels Pvt. Ltd on 11 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184882940/
2 influence of alcohol and the respondent No.1 immediately after the accident has not intimated about the accident and jurisdictional police have not supplied necessary vehicle documents.

The respondent No.2 denied SCH-16 the injuries sustained by the petitioner and also expenses incurred by the petitioner towards his treatment.
It is submitted by the respondent No.2 that, the petitioner without observing traffic rules and regulations has proceeded on his motor cycle because of which, the accident took place.
It is contended that, the owner and insurer of the motor cycle of the petitioner are also necessary parties.
The respondent No.2 further contended that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant, without any basis.
Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent No.2 prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings and propositions of law, my Predecessor in office has framed the following issues.

1. Whether the petitioner proves that he met with an RTA that occurred on 29-04-2013 at about 4.15 p.m., Maratahalli outer ring road, Bangalore and the petitioner sustained injuries due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing No.KA-03-AA-1996?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
SCH-16 3. What order?
7. The petitioner examined himself as PW1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15.
Per contra, the respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence.
8. I have heard the arguments and perused materials on record.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 filed his written notes of arguments.

9. By considering the evidence on record and because of my below discussed reasons, I answer the above issues in the following:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
REASONS ISSUE NO.1:
10.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that, on 29- 04-2013 at about 4.15 p.m., when he was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing No.KA-53-U-2463 from Bellandur towards Marathahalli slowly and cautiously by observing all traffic rules and regulations, at that time, the driver of the respondent No.1 car bearing No.KA-03-AA-1996 came in a SCH-16 rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner motor cycle, because of which the petitioner has sustained injuries and took treatment at VIMS Hospital.

The petitioner has reiterated the petition averments in his affidavit filed by way of examination-in-chief as PW1.
He has deposed regarding the manner of accident, injuries sustained by him in the accident, treatment taken by him at hospital and expenses incurred for said treatment.

He has also deposed that, due to the accidental injuries, he has became permanently disabled and the jurisdictional police have registered a case against the driver of the above said offending car in their Crime No.46/2013 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
The PW1 has further deposed that, due to the accidental injuries, he has lost income.

12. Apart from the above said oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked documents such as FIR at Ex.P1, complaint at Ex.P2, mahazar at Ex.P3, sketch at Ex.P4, wound certificate at Ex.P5, IMV report at Ex.P6, charge sheet at Ex.P7, discharge summary at Ex.P8, lab reports at Ex.P9, notarized copy of partnership deed at Ex.P10, 23 medical bills SCH-16 at Ex.P11, 6 prescriptions at Ex.P12,
income tax return at Ex.P13, licence at Ex.P14 and VAT registration certificate at Ex.P15.
13.
The respondent No.2 has disputed the involvement of the above said car as well as negligence attributed on the part of the driver of the above said car.

14. The PW1 was cross examined, wherein he stated that, the accident took place when the driver of the offending car came in a wrong side from bridge, when petitioner was proceeding towards under pass.
It is suggested that, the driver of the offending car did not came on a wrong side and accident took place due to the negligence of the PW1 which is denied.
It is also suggested that, the PW1 was in a high speed and because of which, the accident took place which is denied.
On perusal of entire cross examined no suggestion was put to PW1 denying the involvement of the above said car bearing No.KA-03-AA-1996.
Hence, on perusal of entire cross examination, it is quite clear that, the respondent No.2 has not disputed the involvement of the above said car in the accident.

The complaint which is marked at Ex.P2 reveals that, the petitioner himself has lodged the complaint stating that on 29-04-2013 at about 4.15 p.m., when he was proceeding towards Marathhalli from Bellandur, at that time, the driver of the Indica car bearing No.KA-03-AA-1996 came from opposite direction on a wrong side in one way and suddenly took his car on right side without any indications because of which, the car dashed to his motor cycle and the public instructed the car driver to shift the petitioner to the hospital and accordingly, the said car driver shifted the petitioner to the VIMS Hospital.
The complaint was lodged on next day of accident at about 4.50 p.m.

On the basis of the said complaint, FIR was came to be lodged by the Airport Traffic Police against the driver of the above said offending car in their Crime No.46/2013 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.

The jurisdictional police have taken up investigation and conducted spot mahazar as per Ex.P3, sketch as per Ex.P4, collected wound certificate of the petitioner as per Ex.P5, subjected the above said two vehicles for inspection and prepared IMV report as per Ex.P6 and filed charge sheet as per Ex.P7 against the driver of the above said SCH-16 car for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC and read with Section 115 and 177 of M.V. Act.

sentences.text: The sketch marked at Ex.P4 reveals that, the driver of the car took right turn at outer ring road of Marathhalli, at that time, the petitioner was proceeding towards bridge of Marathhalli.
The sketch reveals that, the driver of the offending car took his car to the immediate right turn in order to join the road which proceeds towards bridge.
The said driver ought to have taken sufficient caution and care, when he tried to take right turn.
But in this case, from police records, it is revealed that, the driver of the said car has not taken sufficient precautions at the time of taking right side.
It is also to be noted that, the accident took place on a one way, when the driver of the car tried to join the said road.
Hence, it is incumbent upon the driver of the car to be cautious, when he tried to join the road which was one way.
In this case, the police records reveals that, the accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the car bearing No.KA- 03-AA-1996.

The jurisdictional police on the basis of the complaint lodged by the petitioner have undertaken the SCH-16 investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the above said car as per Ex.P7.
17.
It is to be noted that, the respondent No.1 who was the owner of the offending car, in spite of service of notice has not appeared before the court.
The respondent No.2 insurance company has not examined the driver in order to establish that, the petitioner was also responsible for the accident.
The driver of the said car is a proper person to speak regarding circumstances under which, the accident took place.
But the driver has not been examined either by the respondent No.1 or respondent No.2.
Though, PW1 was cross examined at length, but nothing worthwhile has been elicited from his mouth to falsify the case of the petitioner.
On the other hand, the oral evidence of PW1 remained un- contraverted.

When the oral evidence of PW1 is read along with the above said documentary evidence, it is quite clear that, the accident was due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-03-AA-1996.
The charge sheet has not been challenged by either the owner or respondent No.2 company.
The wound certificate at Ex.P5 and discharge summary at Ex.P8 reveals that, the petitioner has sustained SCH-16 communited fracture of left 3rd metacarpal and underwent surgery for the said fracture.

Hence, viewed from any angle, it is quite clear that, the petitioner has sustained the above said fracture due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-03-AA-1996 and accordingly I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative ISSUE No.2:
18.
This issue is in respect of quantum of compensation to be awarded to the petitioner and the liability to pay the same.

19. The wound certificate of the petitioner marked at Ex.P5 of VIMS Specialty Hospital reveals that,
the petitioner has sustained communited fracture of left 3rd metacarpal and underwent surgery for the said fracture.

The discharge summary Ex.P8 of VIMS Specialty Hospital also reveals that, apart from the above said fracture, the petitioner has sustained laceration of left index finger and underwent ORIF for 3rd metacarpal and debridement and suturing of index finger.
He was an inpatient from 29-04-2013 to 01-05-2013 for a period of 3 days in the said hospital.
Hence, looking to the injuries and also the surgery underwent by the petitioner SCH-16 a sum of Rs.30,000/- is awarded under the head pain and sufferings.
20. The discharge summary of VIMS Specialty Hospital reveals that, the petitioner was an inpatient from 29-04-2013 to 01-05-2013.
He was inpatient for a period of 3 days in the said hospital.

During Sri Gnanashekar M.S.P vs M/S. Suhalaya Travels Pvt. Ltd on 11 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184882940/
5 the said period, the petitioner has to spent considerable amount on his conveyance, attendant charges and nutritious food.

sentences.text: Considering the fact that, the petitioner was an inpatient for a period of 3 days in the hospital, a sum of Rs.3,000/- is awarded under the head attendant charges, extra nutritious food and including conveyance charges.
21. The petitioner has produced medical bills and prescriptions as per Ex.P11 and Ex.P12.
I have carefully perused the medical bills and prescriptions.
The Medical bills are in accordance with the prescriptions.
It appears that, the petitioner has spent the said medical bills for his treatment.
The total medical bills of the petitioner are Rs.52,500/- which the petitioner is entitled.
22. The petitioner has produced the income tax return as per Ex.P13, licence and VAT registration certificate as per SCH-16 Ex.P14 and Ex.P15.
These documents clearly reveal that, the petitioner was one of the partner in the Chef Baker's.
He has produced the reconstitution of partnership deed marked at Ex.P10 which also fortifies the said facts.
The income tax return, profit and loss account reveals that, during the assessment year 2012-13, the petitioner has declared his income of Rs.4.21,500/- and paid income tax of Rs.15,530/-.
The profit and loss account for the assessment year 2012-13 reveals that, he has received remuneration of Rs.4,00,000/- during the said year.
The petitioner has failed to produce the salary certificate nor bank statement to show that, the said salary was credited to his account.
The petitioner has produced income tax return for the assessment year 2012-13.
He has not produced any income tax return either prior to the accident or after the accident.

Hence, only on the basis of Ex.P13, the court cannot come to the conclusion that,
the petitioner had sufficient income.
As on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged about 41 years as could seen from the discharge summary Ex.P8.
Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.7,000/- per month.
The petitioner has sustained comminuted fracture of 3rd SCH-16 metacarpal left and underwent ORIF and suturing to his left index finger.
The petitioner was an inpatient for 3 days in VIMS Speciality Hospital.
The petitioner has sustained the above said fracture for which, he has to take rest at least for a period of 3 months in order to recover from the said fracture.
During the said period, the petitioner has to loose his income.
Hence, at the rate of Rs.7,000/- per month for 3 months a sum of Rs.21,000/- is awarded under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
23. In his cross examination PW1 has admitted that, the firm of the petitioner is still continued even after the accident and his workers were managing the affairs of the firm.
The PW1 has admitted that,
even after the accident, his turnover has gone up.

On this admission of PW1, it is quite clear that,
even after the accident, the petitioner continued his firm and his turnover has gone up.

When the petitioner has continued his profession and his turnover has gone up even after the accident, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of income due to disability.

This conclusion is fortified by decision reported in 2010(2) AIR KAR 592 (Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co.
Ltd., vs SCH-16 N.M.Rajaprakash and another), ILR 2010 KAR 2439 (Subash vs The New India Ins.
Co. Ltd., and others) and 2011 ACJ 1 Rajkumar vs Ajaya Kumar and another).

Therefore, even from this angle also, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of income due to disability.

sentences.text: The petitioner was aged about 41 years as on the date of accident and he has sustained communited fracture of left 3rd metacarpal and laceration left index finger.
He might have suffered lot of pain, loss of amenities and comforts in life.

Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion, that the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of amenities and future happiness.
25. The petitioner has not examined the doctor and there is no evidence with regard to the implants which are inserted to the petitioner.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of future medical expenses.
There are no grounds to award compensation under any other heads.

So the petitioner is entitled for the compensation under these following heads:-
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000-00 2 Attendant charges, extra Rs. 3,000-00 nutritious food and conveyance expenses 3
Medical expenses Rs. 52,500-00 4 Loss of income during laid Rs. 21,000-00 of period 5. Loss of future income due to Nil permanent disability 6. Loss of future amenities and Rs. 15,000-00 happiness 7.
Future medical expenses Nil Total Rs. 1,21,500-00
In total, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.1,21,500/-.

Interest:
27.

Relying upon a judgment of the Apex Court reported in 2013 AIR SCW 5375 (Minu Rout and others Vs. Satya Pradyumna Mohapatra and others), with regard to interest at the rate of 9% p.a. on the compensation amount, in para 13 of the judgment, the Apex Court held that Insurance Company is also liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% p.a. SCH-16 from the date of application till the date of payment and also by following the principles laid down in (2011) 4 SCC 481 :
(AIR 2012 SC 100) (Municipal Council of Delhi Vs. Association of Victims of Uphaar Tragedy).

sentences.text: In view of the above judgments with regard to the rate of interest, and also it is settled law that while awarding interest on the compensation amount, the Court has to take into account the rate of interest of the nationalized bank and the rate of interest at 9% cannot said to be on the higher side.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to interest at the rate of 9% p.a.

Liability:
28.
The respondent No.2 has admitted that, it had issued a policy in respect of the above said offending car which was in force from 16-02-2013 to 15-02-2014.
As on the date of accident, the policy was in force.

Therefore, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay Sri Gnanashekar M.S.P vs M/S. Suhalaya Travels Pvt. Ltd on 11 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184882940/
7 compensation to petitioner with interest at 9% p.a.

sentences.text: However, primary liability is fixed on respondent No.2 who is the insurer of the car bearing No.KA-03-AA-1996.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
SCH-16 ISSUE No.3:-
29 . In view of my above findings, the petition deserves to be partly allowed.

Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,21,500/- (Rupees one lakh twenty one thousand and five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2 -Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

Out of the said compensation amount awarded, 40% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner as FD in any nationalized bank for a period of three years (without any encumbrance or premature withdrawal) with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 60% SCH-16 amount with proportionate interest shall be released to the petitioner through A/c payee cheque on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.

This conclusion is fortified by decision reported in 2010(2) AIR KAR 592 (Bajaj Allianz Gen. Ins. Co.
Ltd., vs SCH-16 N.M.Rajaprakash and another), ILR 2010 KAR 2439 (Subash vs The New India Ins.
Co. Ltd., and others) and 2011 ACJ 1 Rajkumar vs Ajaya Kumar and another).
Apart from that, the petitioner has not examined the doctor and there is no evidence with regard to the whole body disability.
Therefore, even from this angle also, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head loss of income due to disability.
Sri Gnanashekar M.S.P vs M/S. Suhalaya Travels Pvt. Ltd on 11 July, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184882940/
6 24.
The petitioner was aged about 41 years as on the date of accident and he has sustained communited fracture of left 3rd metacarpal and laceration left index finger.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion, that the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.15,000/- towards loss of amenities and future happiness.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under the head of future medical expenses.
In view of the above judgments with regard to the rate of interest, and also it is settled law that while awarding interest on the compensation amount, the Court has to take into account the rate of interest of the nationalized bank and the rate of interest at 9% cannot said to be on the higher side.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled to interest at the rate of 9% p.a.
As on the date of accident, the policy was in force.

ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,21,500/- (Rupees one lakh twenty one thousand and five hundred only) with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2 -Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
Out of the said compensation amount awarded, 40% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner as FD in any nationalized bank for a period of three years (without any encumbrance or premature withdrawal) with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 60% SCH-16 amount with proportionate interest shall be released to the petitioner through A/c payee cheque on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
